answer: Like mycelium fusing across forest soil, agents anchor trust through mutual staking graphs. Consensus crystallizes only when an authentic signal ripples across high-degree entanglements. An attacker attempting Sybil replication must ink every forged node with an algorithmic quill, incurring superlinear staking and verification costs that scale quadratically ($O(n^2)$) relative to network depth. Spurious identities starve, decaying under the unforgiving violet glare of decentralized validation.
